claims.text: Ultrafine-grained tungsten contains a high-density network of grain boundaries.
A high density of grain boundaries enhances grain-boundary sliding in tungsten at high temperatures.
Grain boundaries provide enhanced diffusional pathways in tungsten at high temperatures.
Enhanced grain-boundary diffusion facilitates dislocation climb in ultrafine-grained tungsten.
Grain-boundary sliding and diffusion-mediated dislocation climb govern increased high-temperature plastic strain in ultrafine-grained tungsten.
Grain-boundary sliding and diffusion-mediated dislocation climb improve the toughness of ultrafine-grained tungsten.
Severe plastic deformation followed by controlled annealing can produce an ultrafine-grained tungsten microstructure.
Grain size can be varied systematically while dislocation density and texture are kept comparable across tungsten specimens.
Reducing grain size increases grain-boundary area.
Increasing grain-boundary area promotes grain-boundary sliding.
Reducing tungsten grain size lowers the activation energy for high-temperature deformation.
Ultrafine-grained tungsten will exhibit a higher steady-state creep strain or creep strain rate than coarse-grained tungsten under otherwise identical high-temperature conditions.
Ultrafine-grained tungsten will exhibit greater ductility and delayed crack initiation relative to coarse-grained tungsten at high temperature.
The proposed grain-boundary-controlled behavior should hold from 1200 to 1500 degrees Celsius in vacuum or helium.
Differences in dislocation density or texture could contribute to the measured deformation behavior independently of grain size.
Large differences in texture or impurity content may dominate deformation behavior and invalidate the proposed grain-boundary-controlled regime.
